title: Animal matching: VM2 structured output as primary discriminator + MegaDescriptor (BVRA) as tiebreaker
author: jill (operator-directed 2026-09-14, post dog-enrollment + body-scan discussion)
plan_section: v2 animal pipeline completion: enroll operator animals + third-stage embedding model (MegaDescriptor-L-384) for individual animal re-identification, paralleling how face_recognition runs on people after VM1+VM2
trigger: Operator 2026-09-14 (verbatim, directive 1): 'So here is what I am thinking, we already have a well-established pipeline and I do not want to mess with this. I mean, I do not want to mess with changing YOLO vision model 1 or vision model 2, but just like with people, we are going to do basically a third run through of a model and that will be the facial recognition, then with dogs, we can do a third or I guess a fourth run through of the model on this Bohemian animal thing. So it would basically be another add on to the pipeline on the animal branch. So yeah, create some PRD stories for after we get the detailed description of the animal from the VM2 that we then run it into the Bohemian to see if we can recognize enrolled animals.' Operator 2026-09-14 (verbatim, directive 2): 'well that is why I wanted you to look at what the output of VM two said about this dog since it is the only dog that is being enrolled then you can give the option for basically everything with the VM two output has given for the color and type of dog and that will be the match and then we will go to the Bohemian thing to get even better matching.' Operator 2026-09-14 (verbatim, directive 3): 'yes, he is a goldendoodle.' Three concrete gaps in v2: (1) Pipeline Stage 12 only matches vehicles + persons - animal mode falls through with no match and no TG3. (2) No animal matching infra exists. (3) Animal alerts today carry no per-animal metadata beyond YOLO class + animal/dog/0.X. The fix is two-tier: VM2 structured output (species, size, color_pattern, distinctive_features) is the PRIMARY discriminator; MegaDescriptor embedding cosine similarity is the SECONDARY tiebreaker for cases where multiple animals share feature signatures.
background: v2 currently has no animal matching at all. v1 (farm-surveillance-refactor) had a feature-weighted ensemble matcher (animal_matcher.py + animal_schema.py) that scored candidates on distinctive_features + coat_primary_color + body_size + body_build + face_details + coat_pattern + estimated_age + sex_signal. That approach worked but required VM2 to emit a stable, multi-field structured output that often varied alert-to-alert (subjective descriptions). The operator picked a TWO-TIER matching approach (directive 2): TIER 1 - VM2 structured output is the primary match. The operator's verbatim: 'give the option for basically everything with the VM two output has given for the color and type of dog and that will be the match.' TIER 2 - MegaDescriptor (BVRA MegaDescriptor-L-384, https://huggingface.co/BVRA/MegaDescriptor-L-384, loaded via timm.create_model(hf-hub:BVRA/MegaDescriptor-L-384, pretrained=True)) provides 'even better matching' as a tiebreaker for ambiguous cases. Empirical evidence (operator's dog 'Finnegan', replayed through VM2 across 15 alerts today, 2026-09-14): species=dog (15/15), size=medium (15/15), color_pattern={brown: 6, tan: 9} (mixed - set match), breed=null (enum too restrictive), distinctive_features={black collar: 6, curly fur: 3, blue collar: 2, curled tail: 2, ...}. This means the Tier-1 feature signature for Finnegan is: species=dog, size IN {medium}, color_pattern IN {brown, tan}, distinctive_features contains >=1 of {black collar, curly fur, curly coat, curly tail, shaggy fur, curled tail}. The MegaDescriptor tier only activates when Tier-1 returns >=2 candidates within the Jaccard score gap (operator-defined margin). Operator has confirmed: do NOT touch VM1 (YOLO) or VM2 (Qwen-VL). MegaDescriptor weights are downloaded at runtime by timm into ~/Library/Caches/huggingface/hub/ - OUTSIDE the repo (no strip needed).

design_principles: Two-tier matching: TIER 1 - VM2 structured output IS the match (operator directive 2). TIER 2 - MegaDescriptor embedding cosine breaks ties only when TIER 1 returns ambiguous results.

TIER 1 score = w1 * species_match (1.0/0.0) + w2 * size_match (1.0/0.0) + w3 * color_set_overlap (Jaccard) + w4 * distinctive_features_jaccard (Jaccard on lowercase + trimmed). When TIER 1's top candidate has score >= TIER1_ACCEPT_THRESHOLD AND runner_up gap > TIER1_GAP_THRESHOLD, return match without TIER 2. Otherwise, advance to TIER 2.

TIER 2 score = max cosine similarity between MegaDescriptor embedding of the chosen crop and any enrolled animal's averaged embeddings. Threshold default 0.85 (tuned by US-045f). Returns the candidate with highest cosine sim above threshold.

Mirror face_recognition pattern: VM1 (YOLO) detects bbox -> VM2 (Qwen-VL) returns structured description + better_crop -> ANIMAL_MATCHER (two-tier, this PRD) on chosen crop. MegaDescriptor is OPTIONAL tier 2, only invoked when tier 1 is ambiguous.

Better crop selection: pipeline Stage 11b (NEW) reads vm2_result.better_crop, picks crop_a or crop_b accordingly. Falls back to crop_a when better_crop is absent or neither. US-044b builds the pick_alert_image_path() helper that US-045 reuses.

Embedding storage: numpy .npz file with named keys = animal ids, values = stacked 768-dim float32 arrays. Index file = known_animals.json with id + label + species + breed + color_patterns (set) + distinctive_features (set) + first_enrolled_iso + sample_image_paths.
Cosine similarity: standard (A @ B) / (norm_A * norm_B). Threshold initial = 0.85, tuned in US-045f against historical alerts.

animal_matcher.match_animal() returns: {matched: True, candidate: {id, label, species, breed, color}, score: float, gap: float, tier: 1|2, runner_ups: [{id, score}, ...]} on hit, {matched: False, top_candidates: [{id, label, score, tier}], threshold: float} on miss.
Test with synthetic embeddings first (numpy random) before plugging MegaDescriptor - keeps unit tests fast + CPU-only.
Single commit per story on main with US-045 in the message.

stories.title: Add animal_matcher/match.py TIER-1 VM2-feature scorer + TIER-2 MegaDescriptor-cosine tiebreaker
stories.scope: animal_matcher/__init__.py exports match_animal(). animal_matcher/match.py implements two-tier scorer. TIER 1 (always run): score_vm2_features(vm2_animal_structured, enrolled_animals) -> [{animal_id, score, gap_to_next}]. Score formula: w1=1.0 * (species equality: 1.0/0.0) + w2=1.0 * (size equality: 1.0/0.0) + w3=1.5 * color_set_jaccard(vm2.color_pattern, enrolled.color_patterns) + w4=1.5 * distinctive_features_jaccard(lowercase, trim whitespace, /; normalize). Returns sorted by score desc. TIER 1 ACCEPT if top_score >= 1.5 AND top_score - runner_up_score >= 0.5. TIER 2 (only when TIER 1 ACCEPT fails): pick_alert_image_path() (from US-044b, returns chosen crop), compute its MegaDescriptor embedding via infra.animal_embedder.embed_image(), cosine sim vs each enrolled animals {animal_id}__avg vector, return argmax as match if max >= 0.85. Return shape: matched=True -> {candidate: {id, label, species, breed, color}, score, gap, tier: 1|2, runner_ups}; matched=False -> {top_candidates: [{id, label, score, tier}], threshold}. animal_matcher/match_animal.py is the function module US-044c imports. Stage 11b calls pick_alert_image_path() and stores chosen path in pipeline result; US-045d reads it. Also produce docs/animal-matching-design.md with the two-tier flow diagram + worked example for Finnegan (Tier 1 score 3.125, Tier 2 cosine 0.9X). Tests: test_match_animal.py uses synthetic embeddings + fixture enrolled animals + synthetic VM2 dicts to verify both tier 1 happy path (clean match), tier 1 ambiguous (advance to tier 2), tier 2 cosine tiebreak, and unmatched return shape.

stories.notes: Tier 1 weights (w1=w2=1.0 species+size, w3=w4=1.5 color+distinctive_features) chosen so a perfect distinctive_features match (Jaccard=1.0) plus matching species+size gives score=4.0, well above the 1.5 accept threshold. Tier 1 thresholds (ACCEPT 1.5, GAP 0.5) are initial guesses - US-045f tunes them against Finnegan replay output + a held-out dog. Tier 2 cosine threshold 0.85 initial guess - same. match_animal() NEVER loads MegaDescriptor at import time - lazy import inside tier 2 only so tests can run without the model. Storage load: match_animal() opens data/known/animals/embeddings.npz + known_animals.json via animal_matcher/storage.py (US-045c). For unit tests, pass storage dicts directly. Worked example for Finnegan: vm2_result = {species: dog, size: medium, color_pattern: brown, distinctive_features: [black collar]}; enrolled Finnegan = {id: a_dog_finnegan, color_patterns: {brown, tan}, distinctive_features: {black collar, curly fur, curly coat, curled tail}}. Tier 1 score = 1.0 (species) + 1.0 (size) + 1.5 (color Jaccard: |{brown} & {brown,tan}|/|{brown} U {brown,tan}| = 1/2 = 0.5) + 1.5 (dist-feat Jaccard: |{black collar} & {4 features}|/|U| = 1/4 = 0.25) = 1.0 + 1.0 + 0.75 + 0.375 = 3.125. Above 1.5 ACCEPT threshold. If no other enrolled animals, GAP = 3.125 (infinity vs None). Return matched Finnegan, tier 1, score 3.125, gap 3.125.

stories.title: Tune BOTH thresholds (Tier-1 VM2-feature score + Tier-2 MegaDescriptor cosine) against Finnegan replay + held-out dog
stories.scope: scripts/tune_animal_threshold.py: load 15 Finnegan crops from data/known/animals/_staging_finnegan/ + replay VM2 results from data/known/animals/_staging_finnegan/_vm2_all15.json (US-045d fixture). Compute Tier-1 score matrix: each crop's VM2 features scored against (a) Finnegan enrollment signature + (b) a held-out 'other dog' signature (synthetic: different distinctive_features, same species/size/color). Find Tier-1 ACCEPT threshold that cleanly separates Finnegan (top score > 1.5, gap > 0.5) from other dog. Embed all 15 crops via MegaDescriptor-L-384; compute cosine sim vs Finnegan's avg embedding + vs synthetic 'other dog' avg embedding. Find Tier-2 cosine threshold (default 0.85) that cleanly separates Finnegan cosines from other-dog cosines. Output: docs/animal-threshold-tuning.md with two recommended thresholds + reasoning + the actual distribution histograms.
